ethics_check.title: Ethics Approval Check
ethics_check.summary_text: No papers appeared to involve live data collection requiring an ethics approval statement.
ethics_check.report: We did not detect an ethics approval statement, and this paper does not appear to involve live data collection from human or animal participants. Ethics approval is typically not required for theoretical work, simulations, reviews, meta-analyses, or secondary analyses of published data.

power.title: Power Analysis Check

table.text: A difference of this magnitude is similar to or smaller (more conservative) than that considered clinically meaningful in prior airway management trials. 3, 10, 38 Because clinicians choose between these blade geometries for millions of emergency tracheal intubations each year, a high degree of certainty regarding their comparative effectiveness was considered essential; therefore, the trial was designed to provide 95% statistical power. Based on a recent trial conducted in the same ED and ICU settings, we assumed that successful intubation on the first attempt would occur in 85% of patients in the standard-geometry blade group. 3 We calculated that achieving 95% statistical power at a 2-sided α of 0.05 to detect a 5-percentage-point absolute increase-from 85% in the standard-geometry blade group to 90% in the hyperangulated blade group-would require enrollment of 2,350 patients (1,175 per group). To allow for missing primary-outcome data in up to 5% of patients, planned enrollment was increased to 2,500 patients (1,250 per group).

report: We used the LLM model 'vllm/qwen3-8-27b-fp8' to check the contents of 2 paragraphs that contained words suggesting they might contain power analyses. Some essential information could not be detected: software ```{r} #| echo: false # table data -------------------------------------- table <- structure(list(power_type = "unknown", statistical_test = "other", sample_size = 2500, alpha_level = 0.05, power = 0.95, effect_size = 5, effect_size_metric = "other", software = NA_character_), row.names = c(NA, -1L), class = c("tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame")) # display table ----------------------------------- metacheck::report_table(table, "auto", 5, FALSE) ``` ```{r} #| echo: false # table data -------------------------------------- table <- structure(list(text = "A difference of this magnitude is similar to or smaller (more conservative) than that considered clinically meaningful in prior airway management trials. 3, 10, 38 Because clinicians choose between these blade geometries for millions of emergency tracheal intubations each year, a high degree of certainty regarding their comparative effectiveness was considered essential; therefore, the trial was designed to provide 95% statistical power. Based on a recent trial conducted in the same ED and ICU settings, we assumed that successful intubation on the first attempt would occur in 85% of patients in the standard-geometry blade group. 3 We calculated that achieving 95% statistical power at a 2-sided α of 0.05 to detect a 5-percentage-point absolute increase-from 85% in the standard-geometry blade group to 90% in the hyperangulated blade group-would require enrollment of 2,350 patients (1,175 per group). To allow for missing primary-outcome data in up to 5% of patients, planned enrollment was increased to 2,500 patients (1,250 per group)."), row.names = c(NA, -1L), class = c("tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame")) # display table ----------------------------------- metacheck::report_table(table, "auto", 5, FALSE) ``` ::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"} Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size. For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like: > An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group. For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like: > A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5. :::
